The 6,800mAh battery is quite reliable, lasting up to a day and a half with moderate usage, and supports 80W SuperVOOC fast charging. Overall, the OnePlus Nord 5 is a strong contender in its price range, offering reliable performance, a good primary camera, optimised software, and long lasting battery life.

The OnePlus Nord 5 offers notable improvements over last year's Nord 4 model, including a Snapdragon 8s Gen 3 chipset and enhanced cameras. A key design change is the replacement of the alert slider with a new "Plus Key," which can be remapped for various functions, including the new Plus Mind feature.
The Nord 5 runs OxygenOS 15 based on Android 15, offering AI features like Plus Mind, AI VoiceScribe, AI Call Assistant, and AI Translation. It's slated to receive four years of OS upgrades and six years of security updates. The phone features a glass and metal design with a 6.83-inch screen and a substantial 6,800mAh battery.
It features a Snapdragon 8s Gen 3 SoC from Qualcomm, and the handset is the first Nord series phone with an 8-series chip. While not the latest, it's optimised for smooth day-to-day operation and demanding applications. The 6.83-inch Full-HD+ AMOLED screen refreshes at 144Hz and supports up to 1,800 nits peak brightness.
Camera capabilities include a 50-megapixel primary sensor with OIS, an 8-megapixel ultrawide, and a 50-megapixel selfie camera. The primary camera performs well in various lighting conditions, while the ultrawide is decent when there's enough light. It also supports up to 4K/60fps video recording on the main and selfie cameras.
The 6,800mAh battery is quite reliable, lasting up to a day and a half with moderate usage, and supports 80W SuperVOOC fast charging. Overall, the OnePlus Nord 5 is a strong contender in its price range, offering reliable performance, a good primary camera, optimised software, and long lasting battery life.

Buying a mobile in 2026 isn't as easy as it used to be. Thanks to DRAM shortages, phones that comfortably sat below Rs 20,000 just a couple of years ago now cost well over Rs 25,000. What was once considered a mid-range specification now carries a hefty premium, but thankfully, not everything is doom and gloom.
If you're willing to spend close to Rs 30,000, there are still plenty of excellent smartphones worth considering. Every phone on this list comes with at least 8 GB of RAM, fast storage, a smooth high-refresh-rate display, and enough performance to comfortably last several years.
Note: Pricing is accurate as of October 6, 2026, and is subject to change without notice.

1) Motorola G67 Power 5G
Motorola G57 Power Android mobile (Image via Motorola) Price: Rs 24,280 (On Amazon)
If your budget stays around Rs 24,000, the Motorola G67 Power 5G is one of the best recommendations. Motorola has gone with a very simplistic approach and focused on the segments that most buyers actually want: a clean Android experience, excellent battery life, and dependable day-to-day performance.
The Snapdragon 7s Gen 2 processor, 8GB RAM, and 128GB storage are more than enough for social media, streaming, casual gaming, and multitasking. Coupled with that massive 7000mAh battery, this is easily one of the longest-lasting phones in this price segment.

2) Samsung Galaxy F70 Pro
Samsung Galaxy F70 Pro (Image via Samsung) Price: Rs 26,250 (On Amazon)
The Galaxy F70 Pro 5G is the one to pick if you care about the screen and long-term software support. You get a 6.7-inch 120Hz Super AMOLED display, a step up from the LCD panels many rivals use at this price. The 50MP main camera has optical image stabilisation and supports 4K video, making photos and videos noticeably steadier. The 5MP ultrawide and 2MP macro sensors are basic, though.
Performance comes from the Snapdragon 6 Gen 3. It isn't the fastest chip here, but it handles daily use and casual gaming comfortably. A 6,000mAh battery with 45W charging and IP67 protection round out the package. The real standout is Samsung's commitment to six years of OS upgrades and six years of security patches, which is unusual at this price.

3) Motorola Edge 60 Fusion
Motorola Curve screen Android mobile (Image via Motorola) Price: Rs 20,900 (On Amazon)
If your budget starts at the Rs 20,000 mark, the Motorola Edge 60 Fusion can be a great pick for you. Its base 8GB/128GB variant starts at just Rs 900 more than that price mark.
It offers a much sharper curved pOLED display, IP68/IP69 protection, a much more premium design, along with the Dimensity 7400 processor.
As for the cameras, Motorola has ensured buyers get a well-balanced deal without dealing with obvious compromises. Simply put, this is where the premium smartphone experience really starts.

4) OnePlus Nord CE6 Lite
OnePlus Android mobile under Rs 30000 (Image via OnePlus) Price: Rs 28,999 (On Croma)
At almost the same price as the Fusion, OnePlus takes a very different approach. Instead of chasing premium materials, the Nord CE6 Lite doubles down on practicality and real-life use cases. Its 7000mAh battery easily lasts an entire day and often stretches well into the next, while the 144Hz display keeps everything feeling extremely smooth. You can get this if battery life sits at the top of your priority list.

Ralphs (Shipt) is the best value. It has all 12 items for $65.84, which is $2.08 less than Vons ($67.92) and $3.50 less than Target ($69.34).

I sized it for 6 people at about 3 tacos each:
- 3 lb of ground beef
- 60 corn tortillas (2 packs of 30)
- 3 taco seasoning packets
- 2 bags of shredded cheese

The rest is lettuce, tomatoes, onions, sour cream, salsa, limes, avocados and cilantro.

The cart card with the full item list didn't display here. The Shipt product links above are the quickest way to review and check out.
